item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 272319
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, on Hurricane
Nolo, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of the Big Island
of Hawaii, on recently upgraded Tropical Storm Rachel, located
several hundred miles southwest of the Acapulco, Mexico, and has
issued the last advisory on Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys, located
well west of the southern tip of Baja California.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing a large area of showers and
thunderstorms. Recent satellite-derived wind data indicate that the
system is becoming better organized. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for further development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form during the next day or two. The system
should move generally northeastward and remain well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued under
WMO header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued
under WMO header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys Advisory Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...ODALYS IS NOW A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE...
...THIS IS THE LAST ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.8N 123.1W
ABOUT 840 MI...1350 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 20 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys 
was located near latitude 22.8 North, longitude 123.1 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the north-northeast near 6 
mph (9 km/h). The post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the 
north-northeast near 6 mph (9 km/h). A slow northeastward motion is 
expected through tonight, followed by a turn to the south or 
south-southwest.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 45 mph (75 km/h)
with higher gusts. Continued weakening is forecast over the
next couple of days, and this system is expected to dissipate by
the middle of the week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information on the 
post-tropical cyclone please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the 
National Weather Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header 
FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 272038
TCDEP1
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Odalys has lacked organized deep convection for about 12 hours, and 
the system has been a swirl of low-level clouds all day. Therefore, 
Odalys no longer meets the criteria of a tropical cyclone, and this 
is the last advisory on this system. A recent ASCAT-B pass from a 
few hours ago showed peak winds between 35 and 40 kt, and based on 
that data, the initial wind speed is lowered to 40 kt.
 
Strong wind shear, dry air, and cool waters should cause continued
weakening while the system turns southward or south-southwestward
in the low-level flow. Dissipation is now shown by 72 hours, in
agreement with all of the global model guidance.
 
Distant moisture from both Odalys and Hurricane Polo will be
transported into the southwestern United States during the next few
days, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flooding in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 29a
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
535 
WTPZ32 KNHC 272354
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 29A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
500 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...POLO HEADED TOWARD THE BAJA CALIFORNIA PENINSULA...
...CONDITIONS EXPECTED TO BEGIN TO DETERIORATE MONDAY MORNING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM MST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.4N 114.1W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM W OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 200 MI...325 KM SW OF CABO SAN LAZARO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...125 MPH...205 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 355 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...951 MB...28.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, from Punta Abreojos to Santa Fe
* East coast of Baja California Sur, from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
* Mainland Mexico from Guaymas to Huatabampito
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* Mainland Mexico north of Guaymas to Bahia Kino
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia.
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo.
* Mainland Mexico north of Guaymas to Bahia Kino
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, generally within 36
hours.
 
Interests in the remainder of Baja California Sur, and the remainder
of Sonora and northern Sinaloa should monitor the progress of Polo.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM MST (0000 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 22.4 North, longitude 114.1 West. Polo is moving
toward the north near 12 mph (19 km/h). This motion should continue 
through tonight followed by a turn toward the northeast on Monday. 
On the forecast track, Polo is expected to approach the west coast 
of Baja California Sur on Monday, move across the peninsula Monday 
night and then approach northwestern mainland Mexico by early 
Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 125 mph (205 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Polo is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Polo is forecast to be at or near major 
hurricane strength when it reaches Baja California Sur on Monday, 
and it is expected to be a hurricane when it makes landfall in 
mainland Mexico early Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 951 mb (28.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected within the warning area
along the west coast of Baja California Sur by late Monday
afternoon, with tropical storm conditions beginning in the southern
portion of the warning area by early Monday. These conditions are
expected to spread northward and eastward across Baja California Sur
on Monday. Hurricane conditions are expected within the Hurricane
Warning area and possible in the watch area in mainland 
northwestern Mexico early Tuesday with tropical storm conditions
expected to begin Monday night.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 12 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. Rainfall totals of 4 to 6 inches with maximum totals
of 8 expected across portions of Sonora. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of 
southwestern Mexico, west-central Mexico, and Baja California Sur 
during the next couple of days. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please 
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
091 
WTPZ42 KNHC 272050
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
200 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
A NOAA P-3 Hurricane Hunter aircraft was able to complete two fixes 
into Polo earlier this afternoon, indicating the hurricane was more 
or less steady state. In the final fix, the aircraft reported a   
22 n mi closed eyewall, though in the wind data there was some 
evidence of a double wind maximum at 700 mb even though the 
secondary wind max was not seen in the Tail Doppler Radar wind 
data. The peak flight-level winds were 117 kt, which typically 
reduces to 105 kt using a standard 0.9 reduction. However, the 
aircraft did not fully sample the eastern quadrant where higher 
winds may exist. In addition, subjective and objective satellite 
intensity estimates remain at or above 110 kt, so Polo's initial 
intensity will be held at 110 kt this advisory.

Polo is continuing its turn, now moving northward at 355 degrees at 
10 kt. The synoptic setup and track reasoning has not chanced much 
this cycle, with Polo expected to move between deep-layer ridging 
centered over Mexico and a shortwave trough that will soon move into 
California. This trough is forecast to sweep southward, helping to 
capture the smaller Polo, leading it to accelerating to the 
northeast. The NHC track forecast this cycle is largely an update of 
the previous one this morning, though there remains more along-track 
spread, related to Polo's speed of motion, than across-track spread. 
This latest track lies closest to the Google DeepMind ensemble mean 
(GDMI). With the latest update to the track, a Hurricane Warning 
has now been issued for portions of mainland Mexico along the Gulf 
of California. 

Vertical wind shear in the SHIPS guidance is in the 5-10 kt range 
for the next 12-24 h while the hurricane traverses 28-29 C 
sea-surface temperatures, so Polo's short-term intensity will likely 
be controlled by inner-core fluctuations. Given the double wind 
maxima that appeared in the earlier aircraft data, it is not out of 
the question another eyewall replacement cycle (ERC) could occur 
before Polo makes landfall along the west Baja California Sur 
coastline. The latest NHC intensity forecast shows very little 
change in strength before Polo reaches the coast, and the latest 
forecast now anticipates Polo making landfall at near major 
hurricane intensity. In fact, both the 12z HAFS-A/B raw model output 
show Polo making landfall as a major hurricane even if their 
interpolated aids are a bit lower in intensity. Significant 
weakening should occur as it moves over the rugged terrain of the 
Baja California Peninsula, but Polo will likely still be a hurricane 
when it makes its second landfall in mainland Mexico. Rapid 
weakening is forecast thereafter and Polo will likely dissipate 
before the middle of this week over the Mexican Plateau. 
 
Polo is expected to dissipate before it reaches the southern U.S., 
but distant moisture associated with it and Odalys will be 
transported into the southwestern United States during the next few 
days, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash 
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather 
Prediction Center for more information.

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the west coast of the Baja 
California peninsula on Monday as a hurricane, and a Hurricane 
Warning is in effect for that region. Tropical storm conditions 
could reach portions of the coast as soon as tonight or early 
Monday, making further preparations difficult. These conditions will 
likely spread across Baja California through Monday and into 
mainland Mexico on early Tuesday. A storm surge is likely, 
especially in areas of onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja 
California Sur later tonight into Tuesday and portions of Sonora 
late Monday into Tuesday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening 
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.  
Moisture from Polo will support heavy rainfall and flooding 
potential across the Southwest U.S. into the Southern High Plains 
late Monday into Tuesday.
 
3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of
the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next
few days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  28/0600Z 23.2N 114.0W  110 KT 125 MPH
 24H  28/1800Z 25.0N 113.0W  105 KT 120 MPH

 48H  29/1800Z 29.9N 108.7W   35 KT  40 MPH...INLAND

item.description:

000

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS INTO A TROPICAL STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.6N 99.1W
ABOUT 300 MI...485 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 560 MI...900 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 12.6 North, longitude 99.1 West. Rachel is
moving toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A faster  
west-northwest motion is expected during the next few days. On the 
forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to remain well 
south of the coast of southern Mexico. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Steady strengthening is forecast during the next 
few days, and Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane on Tuesday. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Rachel will begin affecting portions of 
southern coast of Mexico during the next couple of days.  These 
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026 
369 
WTPZ43 KNHC 272036
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Recent visible satellite imagery shows that banding features
associated the cyclone remain fragmented, but a couple of ASCAT
passes from just after 1500 UTC revealed an area of 35 kt winds to
the southeast of the center.  Therefore, the system has reached
tropical storm status, making Rachel the seventeenth named storm in 
the eastern Pacific basin this season.

Rachel is moving west-northwestward or 295/4 kt. A deep-layer 
ridge building over Mexico is expected to steer the cyclone 
west-northwest at a faster forward speed through mid-week.  This 
heading should result in the core of the storm passing well south 
of the coast of southern Mexico during the next couple of days.  
After 72 hours, a weakness is forecast to develop in the ridge 
over northwestern Mexico as a trough moves into the southwestern 
United States.  This should cause Rachel to slow, but remain on a 
northwestward to west-northwestward track when it is located well 
southwest of the coast of southwestern Mexico.  The NHC track 
forecast is similar to the previous advisory and lies close to the 
typically reliable consensus aids. 

The SHIPS model continues to diagnose about 20 kt of northeasterly 
shear over the system.  The shear does not appear to be prohibitive 
for strengthening.  In fact, most of the intensity guidance calls 
for gradual strengthening during the next couple few days, and 
Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane on Tuesday. After that 
time, there is uncertainty with regards to SSTs as Rachel may track 
over the cool wake from Hurricane Polo.  As a result, the NHC 
intensity forecast plateaus near the end of the forecast period 
between the Google Deep Mind and HFIP corrected consensus 
solutions.
